criteria.text: Identifies the conflict between the 30-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 45-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 30-day period or aligns the documents.
Calculates the long-stop date as 29 August 2026 (120 days after signing on 1 May 2026) and identifies that expected clearance on 12 September 2026 falls after it, recommending an extension.
States that General Warranty claims must be notified by 29 June 2028 (24 months after Closing) and Fundamental Warranty claims by 29 June 2030 (48 months after Closing).
Identifies that the 5-year SPA non-compete may be unenforceable as wider than reasonably necessary and is inconsistent with the 18-month restriction in the Founder's employment agreement.
Gives the long-stop period as 120 days and as the date 29 August 2026, with days remaining from 12 May 2026 (109 days).
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
Checks whether computed deadlines fall on a weekend and adjusts them under the documents' Business Day definition.
